name.baseName: Autoclaved aerated concrete block, unreinforced, at plant

dataSetInformation.common:generalComment:
Dataset developed within the ARCADIA Project and completed within the agreement between ENEA and MASE. The product was selected in collaboration with the Assobeton Association due to its widespread use in contemporary construction, thanks to features such as lightness, speed, and simplification of installation phases, which make it a more versatile product than traditional bricks used for the same purpose.
For the supply chain study, data were provided by the companies Xella Italia S.r.l. and Ekoru S.r.l.
Dataset developed according to Arcadia project methodology (Report: “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA”). LCA study of autoclaved aerated concrete production (Report: “PRODUZIONE DI ELEMENTI DA MURATURA IN CALCESTRUZZO AERATO AUTOCLAVATO”). The dataset is representative of the national processing technologies commonly used in the unreinforced autoclaved aerated concrete block production.

referenceToExternalDocumentation.common:shortDescription: Viglia, S., Scrucca,F., Cellurale, M., Rinaldi, C., 2025. “PRODUZIONE DI ELEMENTI DA MURATURA IN CALCESTRUZZO AERATO AUTOCLAVATO”. Internal report. For the LCA study background datasets from Ecoinvent database cut-off (v. 3.11) were used.

locationOfOperationSupplyOrProduction.descriptionOfRestrictions: Italy. Dataset representative of Italian production of unreinforced autoclaved aerated concrete block.

technology.technologyDescriptionAndIncludedProcesse:
Autoclaved Aerated Concrete (AAC) elements are mineral-based blocks used in construction. The term “autoclaved” refers to the preparation process: production concludes with curing the material in autoclaves, which enable it to mature under controlled temperature and pressure. AAC is made into bricks containing a high percentage of air, distributed uniformly within small pores, giving the material its characteristic lightness.
After expansion and partial curing in maturation chambers, the material is cut and autoclaved. Sand, ground wet, is mixed with lime and cement to form a fluid paste poured into metal molds, where internal porosity develops. This is due to aluminum powder reacting with calcium hydroxide, releasing hydrogen bubbles that create a foam-like structure. The rising process stops when cementitious binders set, capturing the bubbles while hydrogen is released and replaced by air, a natural thermal insulator.
Once removed from molds, the material is solid but still soft. It is cut into blocks or panels and placed in an autoclave for 11-12 hours. During steam curing quartz sand reacts with calcium hydroxide to form calcium silicate hydrate, which provides the material with its mechanical properties. After autoclaving, the material is immediately ready for use.
For this study, the production phases from grinding to curing were considered, excluding packaging. Use and end-of-life phases are excluded.
Primary data , provided by the companies Xella Italia S.r.l. and Ekoru S.r.l., were collected as physical quantities of materials used in the process as a whole. Background data were modelled according to Ecoinvent v. 3.1.1
Production of equipment and infrastructures is not included, except for the background system

review.common:reviewDetails:
The review was performed in compliance with Arcadia Metodology: “Metodologia per gli studi di filiera della Banca Dati italiana LCA” and ISO 14040-44 norms. The dataset has been assessed limited to the foreground data collected during the supply chain studies.
Each dataset has been evaluated based on the following 4 criteria:
1. Technological Representativeness; 2. Time Representativeness; 3. Geographical Representativeness; 4. Reliability.
In this contest the Reliability is “good”.
review.common:otherReviewDetails: The study was judged by the reviewer as compliant with both ISO 14040-44 and Arcadia methodology.
